summary: Leon is guided by Ria through a vast, dim complex housing Viktor, a giant being whose body is inside the facility. Ria explains the suits are symbolic, that this is the Mark I system after Viktor's accident, and that a Mark II is being built half a mile underground. When Leon asks whether Viktor hunts humans or needs organs, Ria dismisses both as unlikely, and the passage ends as they pass through more rooms toward an airlock guarded by security.
one_line: Ria leads Leon through a vast facility housing Viktor, a giant being whose body sits inside the complex, while explaining its systems and his accident.
key_facts: Ria tells Leon that when Viktor is outside, speaking through his many tendrils or on the phone, he has all the power in the world.
Ria says that inside the facility, Viktor's body is very, very weak, and the suits are there to level out the playing field.
The suits are described as 'all head-games and symbolism' and the current system is called Mark I, jury-rigged after Viktor's accident.
The Mark II system is being built about five miles from the facility and half a mile underground.
When the Mark II is ready, workers will blast a tunnel and take Viktor down into it without compromising the skin of his extended body.
Leon asks what the accident was and whether it was a stroke; Ria answers 'Nothing like that.'
The great room was left over from the original floor-plan when the place was biotech R&D, used for all-hands meetings and small symposiums.
Security protocol dictates no more than ten people in any one space.
Leon asks whether the event was an assassination, and Ria answers 'No.'
Ria says that if Viktor needed an organ, they would make one right there and print it out in about forty hours.
Ria describes the chance that Leon will be harvested or hunted as 'a very low probability outcome.'
A rhythmic whoosh vibration comes up through the floor, which Ria says is Viktor's breath from the filtration systems below.
Overhead, the circulatory system is visible through a grate, with troughs filled with neatly bundled tubes.
The passage ends at an airlock door guarded by a plainclothes security woman, beside a side-room with a glass door full of people watching screens.
